title: Needs of a Living Being
summary: A living organism's needs follow from the kind of organism it is. Man's needs include the use of reason.

lessons.title: What a need is
lessons.objective: Identify a need as something required by the kind of living organism, not a whim or a luxury.

exercises.prompt: On this floor, what is a need of a living being?

choices.text: Something required by the kind of organism it is
Whatever it feels like wanting at the moment
A luxury added after life is already secure
Whatever a crowd votes that it should want

feedback.note: A need is required by the kind of organism. It is not a whim, a luxury, or a vote.

exercises.prompt: Which of these is not a need in this unit’s sense?

choices.text: A passing preference with no tie to the kind of organism
Something the kind of organism requires
A requirement that follows from what the organism is
A requirement of a living being as that kind of being

feedback.note: A preference that does not follow from the kind of organism is not a need on this floor.

exercises.prompt: Match each term to what this floor means by it.

pairs.right: Required by the kind of organism

feedback.note: Need names what the kind requires. Whim and luxury do not.

exercises.prompt: Complete the line for what a need is.

feedback.note: The short form is: a need is something required by the kind of organism. It is not voted in and it is not optional decoration.

exercises.prompt: Build the sentence that names a need.

feedback.note: A need is required by the kind. Whim and luxury are the words this sentence leaves out.

exercises.prompt: Someone says, a need is just a strong wish. What does that miss?

choices.text: That a need follows from the kind of organism
That every wish is already a need
That a crowd decides the organism’s kind
That needs appear only after the organism stops living

feedback.note: Strength of a wish does not make a need. The need follows from the kind of organism.

exercises.prompt: Complete the contrast with a whim.

feedback.note: Calling a need a whim drops the requirement. The kind of organism is what makes the requirement.

exercises.prompt: Build the sentence that ties a need to the organism.

feedback.note: Needs follow from the kind. They are not issued by whim or by vote.

exercises.prompt: Match each claim to the verdict this floor gives it.

feedback.note: Only what the kind requires counts as a need. A wish and an optional extra do not.

lessons.title: The kind sets the needs
lessons.objective: Show that different kinds of organism have different needs, because each need follows from the kind of organism it is.

exercises.prompt: Why do two kinds of living organism not share one list of needs?

choices.text: Needs follow from the kind of organism each one is
Every living thing has the same needs
Each organism picks needs by taste
Living organisms have no needs at all

feedback.note: The list changes with the kind. One shared menu would ignore what each organism is.

exercises.prompt: What goes wrong if you give one kind the needs of another kind?

choices.text: The needs no longer follow from the organism that has them
The needs become more accurate
Needs become optional for every kind
Nothing, because every kind has the same needs

feedback.note: A need borrowed from another kind does not follow from this organism. That is the mistake.

exercises.prompt: Match each idea to the rule about kinds.

pairs.right: Has the needs of that kind
Has a different set of needs
Does not follow from this organism

feedback.note: Each kind carries its own needs. Copying another kind’s list breaks the rule.

exercises.prompt: Complete the rule that sets the needs.

feedback.note: The rule is short: needs follow from the kind of organism. Whim and crowd are not the source.

exercises.prompt: Build the sentence that says kinds differ in their needs.

feedback.note: Different kinds have different needs. They do not share one identical list, and whims are not the name of those needs.

exercises.prompt: A student says every organism needs exactly what a human needs. What is wrong?

choices.text: Needs follow from each kind, not from the human kind alone
Nothing, because kinds do not matter
Human needs are only luxuries
Needs are whatever people agree to share

feedback.note: Human needs belong to the human kind. Other kinds have the needs that follow from what they are.

exercises.prompt: Complete the contrast between kinds.

parts.text: A need of one kind is not automatically a need of
kind, because needs follow from the

feedback.note: Another kind is another set of requirements. The organism, not a whim or a vote, sets them.

exercises.prompt: Build the sentence that states where needs come from.

feedback.note: Each need follows from its kind. Fashion and mood do not set it.

exercises.prompt: Match each error to what it gets wrong.

pairs.right: Does not follow from this organism

feedback.note: The kind sets the needs. A single list, a borrowed list, or no list at all all miss that.

lessons.title: Man's kind, man's needs
lessons.objective: Apply the rule to man: his needs are the needs of the kind of organism he is, not a list taken from another kind.

exercises.prompt: Whose kind sets man’s needs?

choices.text: The kind of organism man is
The kind of organism a plant is
Whatever a crowd prefers this year
No kind, because man has no needs

feedback.note: Man’s needs follow from the kind of organism he is. They are not borrowed from another kind or from a crowd.

exercises.prompt: Why is a plant’s list of needs not man’s list?

choices.text: Man is a different kind of organism, so his needs follow from that kind
It is the same list, because all life is one kind
Man has fewer needs because he is smaller
Plants vote on human needs

feedback.note: The kind differs, so the needs differ. Man’s requirements are the ones that follow from what he is.

exercises.prompt: Match each phrase to the claim about man.

pairs.right: Follow from the organism he is

feedback.note: Apply the same rule: the organism’s own kind sets its needs. Man is no exception.

exercises.prompt: Complete the line about man’s needs.

feedback.note: Man’s needs follow from the kind of organism he is. Plants and crowds do not write that list.

exercises.prompt: Build the sentence that applies the rule to man.

feedback.note: Man’s needs follow from his kind. Whim and fashion are not the source.

exercises.prompt: Someone builds a list of human needs by copying another species. What is the error?

choices.text: Those needs do not follow from the kind of organism man is
There is no error, because kinds share one list
The error is that the list is too short to be a luxury
The error is that feelings were not asked first

feedback.note: A copied list skips man’s kind. His needs are the ones that follow from the organism he is.

exercises.prompt: Complete the rejection of a borrowed list.

parts.text: Man’s needs are not the needs of

feedback.note: Another kind has its own needs. Man’s needs follow from his kind.

exercises.prompt: Build the sentence that names the source of man’s needs.

feedback.note: His needs are the needs of his kind. A mood or a crowd does not replace that kind.

exercises.prompt: Match each wrong source to why it fails for man.

pairs.right: Is not required by the kind
Does not set what the organism is

feedback.note: Man’s needs follow from his kind of organism. Another species, a whim, and a crowd’s taste are the wrong sources.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence holds the lesson?

choices.text: Man’s needs are the needs of the kind of organism he is
Man may take his needs from any kind he likes
Man is a living being and therefore has no needs
Man’s needs appear only if he stops being that kind

feedback.note: The lesson is the rule applied to man: his needs follow from the kind of organism he is.

lessons.title: The need to use reason
lessons.objective: Place the use of reason among man’s needs, as a requirement of the kind of organism he is, not as an optional extra.

exercises.prompt: Which item belongs on the list of man’s needs?

choices.text: The use of reason
The option to skip thinking entirely
The needs of a plant, copied over
Whatever whim is strongest today

feedback.note: Man’s needs include the use of reason. Skipping thought, a plant’s list, and whim are not that need.

exercises.prompt: Why does the use of reason count as a need for man?

choices.text: It follows from the kind of organism he is
It is a hobby some people enjoy
A crowd ordered it as a luxury
It is required of every other kind, but not of man

feedback.note: The use of reason is a need because it follows from the kind of organism man is. It is not a hobby or a luxury.

exercises.prompt: Match each description to the use of reason.

feedback.note: The use of reason is one of man’s needs. It follows from his kind and is not optional.

exercises.prompt: Complete the unit’s line about reason.

parts.text: Man’s needs include the use of
, because that use follows from the

feedback.note: Man’s needs include the use of reason. That inclusion follows from the kind he is, not from whim or luxury.

exercises.prompt: Build the sentence that puts reason on the list.

feedback.note: Man’s needs include the use of reason. Whim and luxury are not substitutes for that need.

exercises.prompt: Someone calls the use of reason a luxury man can drop. What is wrong?

choices.text: The use of reason is a need of his kind, not a luxury
Nothing, because needs are optional extras
The use of reason is a need of plants, not of man
Reason becomes a need only after man is no longer that kind

feedback.note: A luxury can be dropped without touching what the kind requires. The use of reason cannot, because it is one of man’s needs.

exercises.prompt: Complete the contrast with an optional extra.

parts.text: The use of reason is not an optional

feedback.note: Optional extra is the wrong name. The use of reason is a need that follows from man’s kind.

exercises.prompt: Build the sentence that says the use of reason is required.

feedback.note: Using reason is required by man’s kind. It is not optional, and it is not borrowed from another kind.

exercises.prompt: Match each rejection to the claim it answers.

pairs.left: Reason is needed only when whim says so
pairs.right: No: it follows from his kind

feedback.note: The use of reason stays on man’s list of needs. Luxury, exclusion, and whim do not take it off.

lessons.title: Needs in one picture
lessons.objective: Hold the unit in one order: a living organism’s needs follow from the kind of organism it is, and man’s needs include the use of reason.

exercises.prompt: What is the order of this unit?

choices.text: The kind sets the needs, and man’s needs include the use of reason
Whim sets the needs, and reason is left off the list
Every kind shares one list, and reason is a luxury
A crowd picks the kind, then picks the needs

feedback.note: First the rule: needs follow from the kind. Then the application: man’s needs include the use of reason.

exercises.prompt: Which pair does the unit keep together?

choices.text: Needs follow from the kind, and man’s needs include the use of reason
Kinds differ, but man has no needs
Man must use reason, but needs do not follow from any kind
Neither the kind nor the use of reason belongs in the picture

feedback.note: Both claims belong. Dropping either one leaves the unit unfinished.

exercises.prompt: Match each piece of the unit to its place.

pairs.right: Needs follow from the kind of organism
His needs are the needs of his kind

feedback.note: The rule, the application to man, and the inclusion of reason are the three pieces of this floor.

exercises.prompt: Complete the unit summary in your own short form.

parts.text: of organism. Man’s needs include the use of

feedback.note: That is the whole floor: kind sets needs, and man’s needs include the use of reason.

exercises.prompt: Build the sentence that states the full claim.

feedback.note: Needs follow from the kind and include reason, in the sense that man’s needs include the use of reason. Whim and luxury stay out.

exercises.prompt: A review drops the use of reason and keeps only the rule about kinds. What is missing?

choices.text: That man’s needs include the use of reason
Nothing, because the rule never applies to man
That whim is the source of every need
That every kind has man’s needs

feedback.note: The rule about kinds is only half. The unit also says man’s needs include the use of reason.

exercises.prompt: Complete both halves in one line.

parts.text: A living organism’s needs follow from the kind it is, and man’s needs

feedback.note: Include, not exclude. The second half names the use of reason, not a whim.

exercises.prompt: Build the sentence that names both halves for man.

feedback.note: Man’s kind sets his needs, including reason. Excluding reason, or swapping in fashion, breaks the picture.

exercises.prompt: Match each half of the summary to its wording.

pairs.right: Needs follow from the kind it is
His needs include the use of reason
Whim, luxury, or another kind’s list

feedback.note: The summary has two claims and one rejection. Kind sets needs. Man’s needs include the use of reason. Whim, luxury, and a borrowed list do not.

exercises.prompt: Which closing line is faithful to the unit?

choices.text: Needs follow from the kind of organism, and man’s needs include the use of reason
Needs follow from whim, and reason is a luxury of other kinds
Every organism needs exactly what man needs, including nothing further
Man has needs, but they do not follow from the kind of organism he is

feedback.note: The faithful close keeps both halves: the kind sets the needs, and the use of reason is among man’s needs.
